supporting_observations.claim: PowerShell under NWD\ivy.chen created C:\Users\ivy.chen\AppData\Local\Temp\c.zip by compressing \\FILE-NWD-01\Shared\Clients.
Shortly afterward, ivy.chen launched Chrome to quickshare-drop.net.

The proxy recorded a successful CONNECT tunnel to quickshare-drop.net with 51,000,000 client-to-server bytes; Zeek independently recorded about 51 MB outbound from WS-ICHEN-01 to the proxy during the same connection.
The sequence of archiving the Clients share and then sending a large outbound transfer through a browser tunnel to a file-sharing-like domain strongly supports suspected data exfiltration.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records the CONNECT destination and byte counts, but the available records do not expose the tunneled payload or identify which file was sent.
The archive creation is observed, but these records do not establish that c.zip was the file selected for upload.
claims_not_established: The exact contents of the outbound transfer and whether they were the contents of c.zip.
Whether ivy.chen had authorization to share the Clients data with the destination.
Who controlled or received the data at quickshare-drop.net.
additional_evidence_needed: Preserve and examine WS-ICHEN-01 browser history, upload state, and relevant browser artifacts to determine whether c.zip was selected and uploaded.
Obtain the archive's contents and file metadata, plus relevant file-server access records for the source share.
Review proxy or destination-side records, if available, to identify the upload object, account, and recipient; confirm authorization with the data owner and ivy.chen.
unrelated_findings: Cisco AnyConnect's UI was launched on WS-ICHEN-01, although the environment context says there is no VPN and remote administration is limited to WS-SOKAFOR-01. Review separately; these records do not show it caused the alerted transfer. (T039-00190, T039-00191, T039-00192)
